g.text: Two repos in one: gitops-apps/ (app team) and gitops-config/ (devops team)
Real companies split application code and deployment config into two repos. This repo keeps both as two folders with separate pipelines and owners.
test -> e2e (kind) -> build + scan + sign image -> deploy dev
does NOT contain: Helm chart, environments, ArgoCD, cluster credentials
# DevOps team: Helm chart, environments, ArgoCD, platform add-ons, infrastructure, scripts
THE ONLY BRIDGE between the two folders
- name: deploy to dev = commit to Git
images built by apps-ci: ghcr.io/rosaliei/<app>:sha-xxxx | x.y.z
ONE shared Helm chart for every app
.github/workflows/config-ci.yaml: validate + promtool + e2e (runs when gitops-config/ changes)
Where should the Helm chart live? and what changes with two real repos?
shared chart for every app = HOW apps run
B. In each app repo: when an app needs its own special chart
config repo pins the version: many teams
With two real repos, only 3 things change
1. app CI writes to the config repo with a deploy key
(write access to that one repo only)
2. CODEOWNERS becomes repo permissions per team
3. app CI checks out the config repo for the e2e test
"Developers own the code, devops owns how and where it runs.
The only bridge is a commit that changes an image tag,
and ArgoCD only ever reads the config side."
